title: Kendang (gamelan drum)
summary: The kendang is the long conical drum that leads a Javanese or Balinese gamelan. Its big head gives a deep ring and its small head a quick, bright slap, played with the hands and, in some Balinese styles, with a beater. The drummer signals tempo changes and the ends of phrases to the rest of the players.
howToPlay: The drum lies on a woven mat: the big head toward you at the left, the small head to the far right, straps between them.
Dung is the open centre of the big head and Tak a slap at its edge. Tong is the centre of the small head and Ket its sharp edge.
Wood is a tap on the body of the drum.
A ring closes on the place to strike. Strike as it lands.
rules: A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
The patterns count four beats to the bar.
heritageNote: Gamelan players follow the kendang. A change in the drummer's pattern tells the whole ensemble to speed up, slow down or end, so the drum is closer to a conductor than to a beat keeper.
